key_insight: Anisotropic dilation rescales points along their rays in a direction-dependent way, and this simple transform can move between optimal regularizers by acting explicitly on the paper’s radial summary statistic.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical way to adapt a fixed regularization template to data geometry, potentially improving inverse-problem reconstructions and optimization performance.
method: Define anisotropic dilation as a direction-preserving map that multiplies each radius by a positive function on the sphere.
Derive a closed-form profile that transforms a source distribution into a target Gibbs-class regularizer and analyze the induced orbit structure.
Learn the base regularizer and dilation profile jointly, with finite-sample guarantees for linear features and sparse ReLU parameterizations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports positive performance gains in a controlled 2D family and MNIST denoising when the anisotropic profile is learned jointly with the regularizer.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurately estimating and parameterizing the directional profile, so limited data or poorly chosen model classes may reduce the practical benefit.
paper_title: The Geometry of Anisotropic Dilation for Optimal Regularization
